quest.title: The Samsara of the Sabzeruz Festival
quest.description: Now you know very well that this is not the first time you have attended the Sabzeruz Festival. To save Dunyarzad, you must find a way to get to the bottom of the truth.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x450, Mora x18000, Adventurer's Experience x7, Mystic Enhancement Ore x3

chapter.title: The Morn a Thousand Roses Brings

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon remembers everything!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: ...Good, you adapted quickly this time.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: At the end of last night...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We definitely took off our Akasha Terminals last night, but we still heard that beep. Why's that?

choices.text: We've been implanted with another form of the terminals?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But now, we can at least confirm one thing: The Akasha definitely has something to do with whatever's trapping us in this cycle!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon doesn't get it... Why would the Akasha go this far if all it wants is everybody's wisdom?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: It's extremely difficult for lab rats in an experiment to understand why they're being treated the way they are.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If we're lab rats, then what are you? Nahida, you've never told us anything about yourself...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Hmm... I guess I'm the Moon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The Moon? Wasn't that the result of our divination?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Anyway, knowing who I am won't help you get closer to the truth, so you should focus on other things. Don't get distracted and miss any clues~

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay then... Dehya helped us a lot yesterday, so let's go find her. If Paimon's reading the time correctly, those kidnappers should be showing up soon.

choices.text: We failed at severing our connections with them?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Ah, there you are. I've already taken care of those kidnappers. My lady, did you get hurt?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hold on, something's not right...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? Dehya!?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: What's wrong? Why are you both gawking at me like that?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Y—You didn't get hurt this time!?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Huh? What do you mean, "this time"? Why are you so surprised that I managed to get out unscathed? Those kids were amateurs.

choices.text: Aren't you still getting used to your new greatsword?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Shhh... How did you know about my greatsword? I haven't told anyone about it. Please don't tell Miss Dunyarzad!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So Dehya's lost her memories after all...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Anything strange...? You already know that I got a new greatsword. Hmm... if I had to say something, it's weird how such a new weapon could feel so familiar.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: It's as if... I've already used it to fight a countless number of battles.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're saying that although you don't remember using it, your body... feels like it does?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: That's right. Both mercenaries and warriors heavily rely on muscle memory. Only knowing the theory of battle won't get you anywhere.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Traveler, what do you think?

choices.text: Could it be because we removed our Akasha Terminals?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, Paimon's feeling really hopeful!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Is it possible that... we have already broken free?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, you're right! Earlier in the samsara, something like this would've never happened.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We'll know for sure at the end of the day.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: I have no clue what you two are talking about, but it's still dangerous here, so—

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So you want us to take Dunyarzad somewhere else to rest while you check if there are still more kidnappers around. Right?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: How did you know what I was gonna say...? Can you read minds?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Forget it, go and do your thing.

choices.text: Your unfamiliarity usually lands you some scratches.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Phew, it's finally nighttime. Aside from Dehya not getting injured, everything seems to have stayed the same.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Listen, Nahida! We found out that Dehya got out just fine today, even though she got injured every other time she fought the kidnappers.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you think the samsara has been broken? Have we saved Dunyarzad?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Really? Good job on all that progress. Get some good sleep tonight.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, what kind of an answer is that?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: "Tomorrow will come." Everyone assumes this as common knowledge, but the only way you can know that for sure is if you experience tomorrow.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: How many "today"s has it been? Is it possible that "today" will be followed by "yesterday"? Does "tomorrow" truly exist as anything beyond a made-up concept?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: It's even possible that this entire world is a lie, and the history of the whole world has just been one endless Sabzeruz Festival.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, okay, no more! Paimon's brain has already shut down!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Hehe... That's why it makes no sense to waste your energy thinking about things you will learn tomorrow.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Get some good rest! Ya know... Use the bathroom and flush your anxiety dookie away~

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Hold on, what did you just say? Did Paimon hear you correctly?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Hm? People always say they feel a sense of relief after they take a dook-dook. That's why I suggested you could try that. Is that so strange?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh... It's so strange and so against common sense that Paimon is at a loss for words... You were sounding kinda smart just a minute ago!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...We're going to go get some rest.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah... Even though it's happy and lively at the Sabzeruz Festival every day, it feels like it's been a long time since we've really gotten to relax. Let's go back to our room.
*beep*
Continue the harvest. Compared to what we stand to achieve, these sacrifices are trivial.

dialogues.speaker: Guard
dialogues.text: Hey! Stop right there! No one is allowed to enter or leave Sumeru City right now. Go away!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa... Ugh, okay.

dialogues.speaker: Merchant
dialogues.text: *sigh* How am I supposed to conduct business when I'm not allowed to leave the city?

dialogues.speaker: Guard
dialogues.text: Hey! Stop right there! No one is allowed to enter or leave Sumeru City right now. Go away!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa... Ugh, okay.

dialogues.speaker: Amal
dialogues.text: I picked all of these from the forest yesterday, so their freshness is guaranteed!

dialogues.speaker: Kimiya
dialogues.text: This is divine wisdom...

dialogues.speaker: Vihar
dialogues.text: Atten-tion! Any more requests, young soldiers?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: We don't have many more festivals to waste. Hurry and find the truth.
